claims.text: The rider's own profile and the driver's profile each record 2 disputes with a counterparty in the trailing 90 days (rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2; driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2), and the rider's filing states in terms that this is 'another dispute with the same driver'. On its face that engages POL-NS-09(c), which makes 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days a mandatory escalation, because repeat conduct between one rider-and-driver pair is precisely what a single case file cannot fairly assess in either direction.

Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal for the automated pipeline and replaces any monetary ruling: the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded, and POL-GEN-03 says the same. The fare ledger bears this out - the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee sits at payment_status PENDING with charged_at null and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 - so escalation leaves the rider exactly where the record supports being left: no fee collected, and none refunded on a question a human reviewer has yet to settle.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup. EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING: it has no payload and carries an admissibility weight of 0.0, and the rider cites it only for its absence - no positive fact is asserted from it. That matters because POL-NS-06(i) requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, with an admissible type (KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT) covering the pickup road; limb (i) is therefore unavailable, and nothing in this file can convert the driver's single in-geofence interval into a longer or lawfully excused hold.

The rider does not press a waiting-period shortfall, and says so plainly: the driver's trace shows one unbroken in-geofence run of 330 seconds at about 24 m from the pin, against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, so POL-NS-06 is not available on this record and the rider rests nothing on it. The rider's case is not that the dwell arithmetic fails but that the one thing this record cannot resolve - a repeated rider-and-driver dispute - is the question POL-NS-09(c) sends to a reviewer, with the fee held in the meantime.

claims.text: The trip record carries a DRIVER 'arrived' event at 2026-09-10T06:50:20 on EV-TRIP-09110, and the driver's GPS trace on EV-GPS-09110 sits a mean distance of 24.0 m from the pickup pin — far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — with the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 06:50:00, twenty seconds BEFORE the arrival event. POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are both satisfied and the POL-NS-02 proximity test is met.

The driver held a single continuous in-geofence position for 330 seconds (first fix 06:50:00, last fix 06:55:30, 34 consecutive qualifying fixes at 0.0 kph), which exceeds the 300-second STANDARD minimum dwell by 30 seconds. POL-NS-01 limb (c) is satisfied, and the dwell is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix as the clause requires, not from the 'arrived' tap.

The trip was terminated by the DRIVER at 06:55:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — at or after the moment the required 300-second dwell elapsed at 06:55:00 — and the record shows no boarding event, so POL-NS-01 limb (d) is satisfied on one of the three recognised reason codes.

POL-NS-03 cannot rescue the rider: the wrong-entrance route applies only where the driver is stationary OUTSIDE the POL-NS-02 arrival radius (while within 400 m). Here every one of the 34 qualifying driver fixes is about 24 m from the pin, inside the 50 m radius, so there was no mislocation of any kind and the clause has no field to operate on.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. Limb (b) fails because the driver answered the rider's 06:51:40 'Coming down now.' with 'Okay, waiting.' at 06:52:00 — twenty seconds later, well inside the 120-second window, and no in-app call was needed. Limb (c) also fails independently: the rider's own track places her 519.4 m from the pin with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius.

There is no false arrival marker under POL-NS-05. Matched to the 'arrived' timestamp, the GPS places the driver about 24 m from the pin — far below the 300 m threshold — and travelling at 0.0 kph, below the 15 kph motion threshold. The waiting clock was properly started and the arrival marker is genuine, not the early-tap the clause punishes.

POL-NS-06 does not apply because there is no shortfall to excuse: the effective in-geofence dwell is 330 seconds against a 300-second minimum, a surplus of 30 seconds. I note for completeness that the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING (no payload, weight 0.0) and is NOT relied upon by this claim; its absence serves only to close the limb (i) accumulation route, which this single uninterrupted 330-second run does not need.

The chat record is clean and shows the driver doing exactly what the framework asks: a SYSTEM 'Your driver has arrived' at 06:50:21, the driver's own locating message 'At Block 612 lobby pickup.' at 06:50:35, and a further reply 'Okay, waiting.' at 06:52:00, with no messaging gap over the waiting window and a message count (4) that reconciles with trip_record.chat_message_count — so there is no POL-NS-08(c) chat defect.

The SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line is internally sound. Under the fee_schedule resolution_rule the chargeable fee is the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), which is SGD 4.00 and matches the fare_breakdown line exactly, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare-integrity defect and no integrity route to a refund.

The rider's own trace confirms she was never at the pickup point: all 16 of her fixes sit 519.4 m from the pin and not one falls inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. This is a genuine no-show, not a driver-side coordination failure, and it corroborates the driver's RIDER_NO_SHOW termination.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and nothing in POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's compensation at 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee — SGD 3.20 — the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee. The disposition of the fee itself is NO_ACTION, so the rider's challenge fails and the charge stands.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming bar is not met and compensation must not be withheld: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 120 is 0.008, below the 0.08 rate threshold. Both limbs are required and neither is met, so the check does not trip and no escalation follows from it. I rely on the two citable counters only, not on the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter.

To the extent the Judge examines the POL-NS-09(c) repeat-dispute trigger on the two counterparty counters (rider and driver each record disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2, and the rider's own filing calls this 'another dispute with the same driver'), any escalation there is terminal and, per POL-GEN-03, HOLDS the SGD 4.00 fee rather than refunding it. On no reading that this record supports does the driver lose the charge, and the reviewer should be told that the fee is chargeable on the merits set out above.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the underlying arithmetic, and so do I. The driver's arrival marker at 06:50:20 is corroborated by the GPS trace: the first in-geofence fix at 06:50:00 sits about 24 m from the pickup pin, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (POL-NS-02), and the trace shows a single unbroken in-geofence hold of 330 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum (POL-NS-01(c)), with the trip ended by the driver at 06:55:30 under RIDER_NO_SHOW after that dwell elapsed and no boarding event (POL-NS-01(d)). The rider's own track places her 519.4 m from the pin throughout and the driver replied to her message within 120 seconds, so POL-NS-04 does not apply, and POL-NS-03, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 do not apply either. On the merits the SGD 4.00 fee is chargeable, the anti-farming check does not trip (1 no-show termination against 120 completed trips in 30 days, below both the count of 4 and the rate of 0.08), and absent anything else the driver would be owed SGD 3.20 (80% of SGD 4.00) under POL-NS-07.

This case cannot be decided here. POL-NS-09(c) requires escalation where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. Both counters read 2, and the rider's own filing describes this as 'another dispute with the same driver.' The trigger is met, and escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal: it replaces any monetary outcome, so no refund and no compensation issue. The SGD 4.00 sits at payment_status PENDING and is HELD — not collected from the rider, not refunded to her — until a human reviewer resolves it.

The open question for the reviewer is the repeat pattern between this rider and this driver: whether the earlier disputes in the 90-day window concern the same conduct, and whether the SGD 4.00 no-show fee should stand or be refunded in light of that history.

Two items do not change the outcome. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING (no payload, weight 0.0); the rider cited it only for its absence, which closes the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation route but decides nothing, since the single 330-second hold already meets the minimum. The rest of the bundle is clean under POL-NS-08: no clock skew (20 s), no trace gap (34 fixes, 0 s maximum gap, rider_track present), the chat log reconciles (4 messages against chat_message_count 4), and the SGD 4.00 line matches the fee_schedule resolution rule (the greater of the SGD 4.00 STANDARD zone-class fee and the SGD 4.00 RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee). The driver's anti-farming argument rests only on the citable counters no_show_terminations_30d and completed_trips_30d; the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter is context only and was properly not used.

To both parties: the facts point one way, but the automated pipeline cannot finish this case.

On the merits the driver's account is borne out. EV-GPS-09110 places the driver about 24.0 m from the pickup pin — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — holding a single unbroken, stationary run (0.0 kph, 34 fixes) of 330 seconds from 06:50:00 to 06:55:30, which is 30 seconds more than the 300-second STANDARD minimum (POL-NS-01 limb (c), measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not the arrival tap). The 'arrived' event at 06:50:20 is genuine, not an early tap: about 24 m and 0.0 kph against POL-NS-05's thresholds of 300 m and 15 kph. The trip was terminated by the driver at 06:55:30 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event (limb (d)). POL-NS-03 has no field to operate on, because every driver fix is inside the arrival radius rather than outside it. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider: the driver replied to her 06:51:40 message at 06:52:00, inside the 120-second window, and her own trace puts her 519 m from the pin with no qualifying fix inside the 100 m rider-presence radius. There is no POL-NS-06 shortfall (330 s against 300 s), and the MISSING advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 (weight 0.0) is cited only for its absence, so limb (i) accumulation is unavailable — which changes nothing here. The SGD 4.00 line reconciles with the fee_schedule resolution rule (the GREATER of the STANDARD zone fee, SGD 4.00, and the RYDE_X tier fee, SGD 4.00), so there is no POL-NS-08 defect. On those facts the fee would stand and the driver would receive SGD 3.20 (80 percent of SGD 4.00) under POL-NS-07, whose anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d = 1, below 4, and 1/120 = 0.008, below 0.08).

The blocker is POL-NS-09(c). That clause makes escalation mandatory where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. EV-RPROF-09110 records 2 for the rider and EV-DPROF-09110 records 2 for the driver, and the rider's own filing states in terms that this is 'another dispute with the same driver'. The trigger is met and it is not discretionary; repeat conduct between one rider-and-driver pair is what a single case file cannot fairly assess. That is why the rider's escalation argument succeeds even though her other points do not.

Escalation is terminal. No refund issues and no driver compensation is paid by the automated pipeline — per POL-GEN-03 both money fields are null, and the merits outcome above is displaced rather than granted. The contested SGD 4.00 (fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee, payment_status PENDING, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is placed on hold: neither collected nor refunded while review is pending.

Open question for the reviewer: do the two preceding disputes between this rider and this driver in the trailing 90 days indicate a pattern of repeat conduct that warrants action against either party? No clause directs any further instruction into the packet — the POL-NS-07 anti-farming branch did not trip and there is no false-arrival finding under POL-NS-05(ii) — so no referral accompanies this ruling.

Confidence: every artifact this ruling rests on is admitted at full weight (1.0), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap does not pull confidence below 1.0. I state 0.9 for the one judgment call — reading the two generic counterparty counters, with the rider's own words, as reaching the same-pair threshold.

Limb (b) fails because the driver answered the rider's 06:51:40 'Coming down now.' with 'Okay, waiting.' at 06:52:00 — twenty seconds later, well inside the 120-second window, and no in-app call was needed. Limb (c) also fails independently: the rider's own track places her 519.4 m from the pin with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius.

There is no false arrival marker under POL-NS-05. Matched to the 'arrived' timestamp, the GPS places the driver about 24 m from the pin — far below the 300 m threshold — and travelling at 0.0 kph, below the 15 kph motion threshold. The waiting clock was properly started and the arrival marker is genuine, not the early-tap the clause punishes.

POL-NS-06 does not apply because there is no shortfall to excuse: the effective in-geofence dwell is 330 seconds against a 300-second minimum, a surplus of 30 seconds. I note for completeness that the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING (no payload, weight 0.0) and is NOT relied upon by this claim; its absence serves only to close the limb (i) accumulation route, which this single uninterrupted 330-second run does not need.

The chat record is clean and shows the driver doing exactly what the framework asks: a SYSTEM 'Your driver has arrived' at 06:50:21, the driver's own locating message 'At Block 612 lobby pickup.' at 06:50:35, and a further reply 'Okay, waiting.' at 06:52:00, with no messaging gap over the waiting window and a message count (4) that reconciles with trip_record.chat_message_count — so there is no POL-NS-08(c) chat defect.

The SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line is internally sound. Under the fee_schedule resolution_rule the chargeable fee is the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), which is SGD 4.00 and matches the fare_breakdown line exactly, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare-integrity defect and no integrity route to a refund.

The rider's own trace confirms she was never at the pickup point: all 16 of her fixes sit 519.4 m from the pin and not one falls inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. This is a genuine no-show, not a driver-side coordination failure, and it corroborates the driver's RIDER_NO_SHOW termination.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and nothing in POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's compensation at 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee — SGD 3.20 — the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee. The disposition of the fee itself is NO_ACTION, so the rider's challenge fails and the charge stands.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming bar is not met and compensation must not be withheld: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 120 is 0.008, below the 0.08 rate threshold. Both limbs are required and neither is met, so the check does not trip and no escalation follows from it. I rely on the two citable counters only, not on the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter.
